executive_summary: Markets face a triple threat on Wednesday: Iran's overnight ballistic missile salvo on US bases — successfully intercepted but triggering a 5% oil spike and US-Saudi counter-strikes in Iraq — has reignited Strait of Hormuz supply fears just as the deepening semiconductor selloff enters its fourth day on China's DUV lithography breakthrough. The Fed announces at 2pm ET with Chair Warsh expected to hold at 3.50-3.75% but lean hawkish given the fresh inflationary impulse from energy prices. The silver lining: Microsoft, Meta, Qualcomm, ARM, and Lam Research report after the bell, and a blowout Azure print could arrest the tech rout. Trade the defense/energy long, semiconductor short duality until earnings clarity arrives.

macro_events.title: Iran Surprise Ballistic Missile Attack on US Military Bases
macro_events.causal_chain: IRGC launches multiple ballistic missiles at US bases in Jordan > US CENTCOM intercepts all missiles > US and Saudi air forces conduct counter-strikes on Iran-aligned targets in eastern Iraq > Strait of Hormuz transit risk premium rises (21% of global oil trade, 20% of LNG) > Brent spikes 5% to $87.53, WTI to $83 > War-risk insurance premiums spike on VLCCs > Asian refiners begin contingency routing via Cape of Good Hope (+12-14 days, +$2M/trip) > Qatar LNG to Europe at risk > Inflation expectations tick up > 10Y yield under upward pressure > Fed rate-cut probability compressed further
macro_events.geographic_dimension: Middle East > Strait of Hormuz > Global oil/LNG trade > Asia-Pacific refiners > European energy markets
macro_events.historical_analog: January 2020 Soleimani assassination — Brent spiked 4% intraday, defense stocks (LMT, RTX) rallied 3-5% over one week, airlines fell 2-3%. September 2019 Abqaiq attack — Brent +15% in 24h, tanker rates surged 20-35% in one week.
macro_events.counterargument: Previous Iran-US exchanges this month have been followed by de-escalation pauses; market may be desensitized to intercepted attacks. Oil is already 6% off recent highs after last week's pause. Saudi-Omani diplomatic channel remains open.

macro_events.title: China DUV Lithography Breakthrough Triggers Global Semiconductor Rout
macro_events.causal_chain: Shanghai-based Yuliangsheng Technology begins mass production of DUV lithography machines > threatens ASML monopoly on immersion DUV equipment > SMIC, Hua Hong, CXMT can source domestic equipment > US export controls lose primary chokepoint leverage > Western semi equipment companies (ASML, AMAT, LRCX, KLAC) face China revenue risk and moat erosion > South Korean memory giants Samsung (-13%) and SK Hynix (-15%) face new competition from Chinese fabs at mature nodes > SOX index enters correction territory > Contagion spreads to entire AI/chip complex including NVDA (-5%), AMD (-8%), MU (-6%)
macro_events.geographic_dimension: China (domestic capability) > South Korea (KOSPI -11%) > Netherlands (ASML) > US semiconductor ecosystem > Global tech indices
macro_events.historical_analog: Huawei Mate 60 Pro launch (Sep 2023) — proved China could make 7nm chips despite sanctions, triggered semi equipment selloff. The DUV breakthrough is more significant because it targets manufacturing equipment itself, not just end products.
macro_events.counterargument: DUV mass production does not equal EUV capability; China remains 2-3 nodes behind in leading-edge logic. Yuliangsheng yields and reliability at scale are unproven. ASML EUV business (which China cannot replicate) is the real growth driver.

affected_tickers.reason: Direct monopoly threat from Chinese DUV equipment; China revenue at risk of zero

macro_events.title: Fed FOMC Decision — Warsh 2nd Meeting as Chair
macro_events.causal_chain: Fed announces at 2pm ET > expected to hold at 3.50-3.75% (5th consecutive hold) > no dot plot or SEP this meeting > all signal comes from Warsh 2:30pm press conference > Warsh known to favor less forward guidance and has hawkish tendencies > fresh oil spike from Iran attack gives ammunition to inflation hawks > any hawkish language on inflation persistence > rate-cut expectations pushed out further > growth stocks re-priced lower > 10Y yield pushes toward 4.70% > DXY strengthens > EM currencies weaken
macro_events.geographic_dimension: US monetary policy > global risk assets > EM currencies > commodity-importing nations
macro_events.historical_analog: Warsh first meeting (June 2026) — held steady but subtle language shift caused 50bps of rate-cut repricing over two weeks.
macro_events.counterargument: June CPI fell 0.4% (largest monthly decline since April 2020), with core at 2.6% YoY approaching 2% target. Warsh may acknowledge disinflation progress. The oil spike is supply-driven, not demand-driven — Fed may look through it.

macro_events.title: NVIDIA-OpenAI $250B Financing Guarantee Raises AI Bubble Fears
macro_events.causal_chain: NVDA negotiates $250B guarantee for OpenAI 10-GW Ohio campus > signals OpenAI cannot obtain investment-grade rating alone > creates circular dependency: NVDA sells chips to OpenAI, NVDA guarantees the debt to buy those chips > if OpenAI fails lease payments, NVDA absorbs $250B liability > market questions whether AI capex is being financed by the same companies that benefit from it > broader circular financing narrative feeds into chip selloff > total NVDA exposure could reach $600B on a single customer
macro_events.geographic_dimension: US — Silicon Valley / Ohio data center corridor
macro_events.historical_analog: SoftBank Vision Fund circular investments in WeWork (2019) — vendor financing its own customer to sustain revenue growth.
macro_events.counterargument: NVDA has $45B+ in cash and $130B+ annual revenue; $250B guarantee is contingent, not cash outflow. If AI demand is real, OpenAI will service its debt. The deal signals confidence in AI demand trajectory.
